paper.title: Efficient Multi-objective Prompt Optimization via Pure-exploration Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Best feasible prompt identification (linear constrained bandit, fixed budget)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards: two-dimensional reward vector with a feasibility constraint on the second objective.
unmapped: Two-dimensional reward vector mu(x) = (phi(x)^T theta1, phi(x)^T theta2); target is the arm maximizing mu_1 subject to mu_2(x) >= tau (known threshold tau)
Independent sigma-sub-Gaussian noise on each objective
settings.definition_quote: In the linear constrained bandit setting, we assume the number of reward dimensions is only two for simplicity and the expected rewards satisfy the linear structure, \mu_1(x)=\phi(x)^\top \theta^{(1)},\ \mu_2(x)=\phi(x)^\top \theta^{(2)} ... \eta^{(t)}_1, \eta^{(t)}_2 are the independent \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise. ... x^\star := \arg\max_{x\in\mathcal{F}} \mu_1(x).

algorithms.name: Linear Constrained Sequential Halving (Gensec with SH scheduler, G-optimal design allocator, least-squares estimator)

symbols.H_c: max over x != x* of 1/Delta(x)^2, with constrained gap Delta(x) = min{max(tau - mu_2(x), mu_1(x*) - mu_1(x)), mu_2(x*) - tau}

conditions: T >= 45 d ceil(log2 K) (paper's budget B is T)
at least one feasible arm exists
linear rewards for both objectives with independent sigma-sub-Gaussian noise
tuning: Scheduler: Sequential Halving, R = ceil(log2 K), n_r = floor(B/R)
Allocator: G-optimal design (mirror descent + rounding, kappa in (0,1/3])

source.label: thm:LCSR_formal
source.quote: Given a fixed set of $K$ arms $\mathcal{X}$ with the linear reward structure specified in \Cref{eqn:thm2:1,eqn:thm2:2}, under total budget $B \geq 45 d \left\lceil \log_2 K \right\rceil$, the probability that \Cref{alg:LCSR_formal} fails to output the best feasible arm is upper bounded by \[ \mathbb{P}( 1 \notin A_R) \le 48 \left\lceil \log_2 K \right\rceil \exp\left( -\frac{a}{4 } \cdot \left\lfloor\frac{B}{\left\lceil \log_2 K \right\rceil}\right\rfloor \cdot \frac{1}{dH}\right), \] where a = 1/(6\sigma^2), H = \max_{x \in \mathcal{X}\setminus\{1\}}\frac{1}{\Delta^2(x)}

results.notes: Theorem 1 (thm:LCSR) is the informal version of this result, with an unspecified constant c_1 in place of a/4; it is not recorded separately. The paper's budget B is mapped to T. The setting is out of scope because the rewards are vector-valued. In Lemma 3 the proof bounds l_{r-1}/l_r by 4 without justification; the bound is recorded as stated.
